record.paper_title: Negative Circles in Signed Graphs: A Problem Collection
record.original_question: Given a signed graph Σ, find a largest possible family of pairwise vertex-disjoint negative circles in Σ.

evidence.quote: P2. Find a maximum set of pairwise disjoint negative circles.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A signed graph is a pair Σ = (G, σ) where G = (V, E) is a finite graph (loops and multiple edges allowed) and σ : E → {+1, −1} is a sign function on its edges. A circle (simple closed walk) C in G is called negative if the product of the signs of its edges is −1, and positive otherwise. Two circles are said to be vertex-disjoint if they share no vertex.

Problem: Develop a method, structural characterization, or formula that, given an arbitrary signed graph Σ, determines a family of pairwise vertex-disjoint negative circles in Σ of maximum possible cardinality (equivalently, determine the maximum number ν⁻(Σ) of pairwise vertex-disjoint negative circles).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of finding a maximum family of pairwise vertex-disjoint negative circles in a general signed graph is stated as an open problem in the signed-graph problem collection and is reiterated as open in subsequent work. Partial results exist for restricted classes (e.g., antibalanced planar signed graphs of negative girth at least 5, signatures-packing, two-circle cases by Slilaty, and algorithmic results by Hochstättler et al.), but no general solution is known.

status_evidence.title: Packing Signatures in Signed Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Maximum family of disjoint negation sets / signatures.
status_evidence.claim: Related packing variants have been studied; the negative-circle packing problem in general remains unresolved.
